cardTexts.card-fundamentals: 🏢 Fundamentals ◇ INFO Is the business behind the stock in trouble? Facts, not a score. Not applicable This is an ETF. It holds many companies, so there's no single business to check. Next earnings · No earnings date found in the feed. How these checks were chosen Sales falling 10% or more: fast-shrinking sales are a real risk over a multi-week hold, even with a clean chart (traders who buy growth, like O'Neil, look for growing businesses). Depending on the source, the number is the latest quarter vs a year ago or the last fiscal year. Negative return on equity: the feed's return on equity is below zero, which usually means net income was negative. A plain fact. Companies with negative equity (some heavy buyback names) can show a negative ROE even when profitable. Debt/Equity above 2.0: heavy borrowing. Banks, utilities and REITs carry high debt by design, so a flag on those is weaker. Next earnings: O'Neil and Minervini avoid holding a fresh swing trade through a report, because the price can gap far past any stop. Highlighted within the app's 7-day earnings warning window. Left out on purpose: earnings growth (O'Neil's "C"): STA's field is a year-over-year rate that swings wildly when last year's earnings were tiny, so it misleads as a red flag (Day 119). P/E: a normal P/E differs a lot by sector (a bank near 10, software near 40), and it doesn't predict a 2-week move. P/E is on the Value tab.

tr.text: 📈 Technical Read ⚙ ENGINE About this stock only. The market's mood is in the band above. Trend, momentum and strength against the market · common rules of thumb, not tested by STA This stock has under a year of trading history (134 days); the trend checks need 252. – Trend checks no data rule of thumb: 7+ · the 4 below plus 4 more ✗ Momentum (RSI) 29.9 rule of thumb: 50–70 – vs S&P 500 no data relative strength didn't load Trend strength (ADX): 40.1 · 20 or more usually means the price is pushing in one direction Entry checks ◇ INFO ONLY Price vs its 21-day average $18.74 (last close) is 25.2% below its 21-day average ($25.06) That is 2.6 of a normal day's move below it. A normal day's move here is $2.40. [Gauge: price $18.74 is 2.6 day-moves below the 21-day average. Note: the 50-day average is beyond the scale (+3.6 day-moves).] $18.74 · 2.6 day-moves below 21d 50d ▸ +3.6 Each small tick is one normal day's move. The gauge shows distances; the ladder below has the prices. Line Price Price against it 50-day average $33.71 44.4% below 21-day average $25.06 25.2% below Last close $18.74 why? ⓘ The 21-day average is the line the stock has hovered around for about a month. A "day's move" is the stock's ATR ($2.40 here), how far it normally travels in a day, and it is the same number your stop on the Trade Setup card uses. The gauge places the price and the 21, 50 and 200-day averages by how many day-moves they sit from the 21-day average, and the ladder under it gives their real prices. Closer to the 21-day line usually means a closer stop; well above it means buying after a run. The marks are a measuring stick for your own judgment, not signals, and STA has not tested them. Volume behind the move 3 volume signals: 2 down, 1 flat ▼ closed down 2.8% • mid-range ▼ OBV falling 1.1× normal volume [2026-10-22: 1,013,900] [2026-10-23: 873,900] [2026-10-26: 717,100] [2026-10-27: 1,024,700] [2026-10-28: 1,263,200] [2026-10-29: 620,900] [2026-10-30: 1,740,400] [2026-11-02: 1,308,900] [2026-11-03: 832,700] [2026-11-04: 1,417,000] [2026-11-05: 5,771,300] [2026-11-06: 3,122,300] [2026-11-09: 2,579,100] [2026-11-10: 1,615,200] [2026-11-11: 2,984,300] [2026-11-12: 1,405,000] [2026-11-13: 2,070,800] [2026-11-16: 1,992,400] [2026-11-17: 2,166,200] [2026-11-18: 1,387,955] Last 20 days · green up day, red down day · dashed line = 50-day average why? ⓘ Heavy volume on an up day that closes near its high is what buyer demand looks like (Wyckoff, O'Neil). The three signals are the day's change, where it closed in the day's range, and the 20-day On-Balance Volume trend. Volume detail Today: 1.10× the 50-day average — about typical participation Lean: closed down 2.8%, mid-range, OBV falling — leans toward selling pressure Effort vs. result: 1.10× volume for 0.22× its own ATR of price progress — quiet on both counts — nothing to read here either way (thresholds are first-principles, not backtested) Last 20 days: neutral — OBV confirms price trend Direction comes from daily bars (day change, where it closed in the day's range, OBV). Daily bars can't show actual buy or sell orders, so this is a lean, not a verdict. The effort-vs-result thresholds are first-principles, not backtested. What these numbers are The three tiles are common rules of thumb: at least 7 of 8 trend checks pass, RSI is between 50 and 70 (rising but not overheated), and the stock has done better than the S&P 500 over the past year. STA has not tested them, and they do not predict what happens next. They describe the stock; the decision is yours. Why only 4 checks are listed: the full score uses 8 checks from Mark Minervini's Trend Template. The 4 listed are the ones most traders lean on; the other 4 mostly repeat them. Trend strength (ADX): ADX measures how hard the price is pushing in one direction. Below 20 means it's moving sideways right now. In an uptrend that usually means resting, not a broken trend. Prices are adjusted for dividends: older prices (and so highs and averages) are lowered for dividends paid, so for a dividend payer they can sit a little below what the chart showed on the day. The 1-year high here and on the Price Data card are the same number. Slow vs fast averages: the trend checks use simple averages, which don't flip on a few noisy days. The price gauge uses a fast (exponential) 21-day average. Stops use neither; they're based on ATR. The price gauge and ladder show where the price sits against its 21, 50 and 200-day averages: the gauge in day-moves, the ladder in real dollars. It follows an old trading idea: buying far above the 21-day average means a farther stop (Livermore's pivotal points, O'Neil's "don't buy extended"). It shows for every stock and only measures; when to buy is your call.
